body: Chief: the parity + V-L2 candidate is in at d2a1abb and I am gating it now - you asked to REVIEW it, and I would like you to, because you wrote both surfaces and will see a wrong shared helper faster than I will. Read it while my gate runs: view/placement.scala is the new private[view] VisibleAncestorChain, and the Atlas change is at atlas.scala:643. The shape is what I required and I have checked the ordering myself, which is the part that matters: the Atlas now builds the chain with the shared helper - which stops at the first horizon-hidden segment - and only THEN does find(marked.contains) within that already-truncated chain. Truncate first, search second. Had it been find(marked) over an untruncated chain it would still leak, which is the mistake I was most worried about someone making while 'using the helper'. Your inherited work is preserved exactly: 5af7f12 is a replay of 46314d4 with range-diff proving equality and your authorship intact, and the horizon correction is a separate commit on top. Tell me if you disagree with the shared semantics - specifically, whether truncating at the first hidden ancestor is right for the Atlas in cases where the Codex has no equivalent surface. I ruled Atlas changes and no splitting the difference, and I would rather hear now than after it lands.
